en.title: British Airways Boeing 787-10 veers off taxiway at Heathrow, stuck in mud
en.summary: A British Airways Boeing 787-10 veered off a taxiway at London Heathrow on the morning of November 17, its nose wheel stuck in the mud while taxiing for departure to Lagos as flight BA75; the cause is unknown and the return leg has been canceled.
body: A British Airways Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner has suffered a taxiway excursion at London Heathrow Airport (LHR). The widebody twinjet had pushed back from its gate at the airport's satellite Terminal 5C and was on its way to runway 27L ahead of its planned departure to Murtala Muhammed International Airport (LOS) in Lagos, Nigeria, as BA75. However, it missed a turn and got stuck. Several hours later, the aircraft remained beached in the grass at the western end of runway 27L between satellite terminals 5B and 5C. British Airways has confirmed that it is working to get the passengers of flight BA75 on their way again, but the return leg has been canceled as a result of the excursion.

The incident involved British Airways flight BA75, operated by G-ZBLF. Heathrow's website shows it pushed back at around 10:30 AM local time ahead of what should have been a six- to seven-hour flight to Nigeria. According to flight tracking data, at 10:45 AM local time it failed to make its planned turn as it headed to the runway. After emerging at the southern end of the taxiway that bisects satellite terminals 5B and 5C, G-ZBLF attempted a left turn to head east to the far end of runway 27L, but while taxiing at around five knots (9.3 km/h), it only partially managed the turn before its nose wheel got stuck in the mud. The cause of the taxiway excursion remains unknown. A British Airways spokesperson told Simple Flying: "We're very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right."

According to fleet data from ch-aviation, G-ZBLF is one of 14 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners British Airways currently has at its disposal. These aircraft are just 3.8 years old on average, compared with a fleet-wide mean of 13.2 years. BA has another 36 units of the 787-10 on order, meaning it will eventually fly 50 examples, and it also operates 12 Boeing 787-8s and 18 787-9s. G-ZBLF is one of BA's older 787-10s at 5.56 years old; ordered in December 2013, it first flew in April 2021 and was delivered to BA in September 2022, the third 787-10 to reach the airline. BA configures its 787-10s with 256 seats: eight First suites, 48 Club World business-class flatbeds, 35 World Traveller Plus premium economy recliners and 165 World Traveller economy seats.

BA75 is a daily scheduled service from London Heathrow to Lagos, with a scheduled departure of 10:10 AM and a block time of six hours and 45 minutes, arriving at 5:55 PM. According to Cirium, British Airways serves this route daily in both summer and winter using the Boeing 787-10. Competition comes from Virgin Atlantic and Air Peace, although the latter flies from Gatwick instead. Elsewhere in Nigeria, BA also flies daily from Heathrow to Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (ABV) in Abuja using older Boeing 777 widebodies.

facts.claim: A British Airways Boeing 787-10 operating flight BA75 suffered a taxiway excursion at London Heathrow after pushing back at around 10:30 AM local time for departure to Lagos.

At 10:45 AM local time the aircraft failed to make its planned turn and its nose wheel got stuck in the mud at the western end of runway 27L between satellite terminals 5B and 5C, while taxiing at around five knots.
British Airways confirmed it is working to get BA75 passengers on their way again, and the return leg from Lagos has been canceled.
G-ZBLF is one of 14 Boeing 787-10s in British Airways' fleet, 5.56 years old and delivered in September 2022; BA has 36 more 787-10s on order and also operates 12 787-8s and 18 787-9s.
BA75 is a daily scheduled service from London Heathrow to Lagos with a scheduled departure of 10:10 AM and a block time of six hours and 45 minutes.

zh.title: 英國航空787-10客機滑出滑行道受困草地、拉各斯航班取消
zh.summary: 英國航空一架波音787-10客機17日上午在倫敦希斯洛機場滑行時錯過轉彎，前輪陷入草地受困，執飛的拉各斯航班BA75延誤、回程航班取消；原因仍不明，英航表示正協助旅客改搭其他航班。
body: 英國航空一架波音787-10夢幻客機17日上午在倫敦希斯洛機場（LHR）滑行時衝出滑行道。該機執飛前往奈及利亞拉各斯的BA75航班，約上午10時30分由5號航站C衛星樓登機門後推，前往27L跑道途中錯過轉彎而受困。據航班追蹤資料，飛機於當地時間上午10時45分左右未能完成預定轉彎，以約5節（每小時9.3公里）的速度滑行時，前輪陷入泥地，停在27L跑道西端、5B與5C衛星樓之間的草地上，數小時後仍受困於原地。事故原因目前仍不明。

英國航空已證實正協助BA75航班的旅客繼續行程，並對造成的不便致歉；受此影響，由拉各斯返回倫敦的回程航班已經取消。涉事飛機註冊編號G-ZBLF，是英航14架787-10之一，機齡5.56年，2022年9月交付，為英航接收的第3架787-10。英航另訂購36架787-10，未來5隊將達50架；此外還營運12架787-8與18架787-9。該機採7低密度布局，共256個座位，包括8間頭等套房、48個Club World商務艙平躺座椅、35個World Traveller Plus特選經濟艙座椅與165個經濟艙座位。
BA75是倫敦希斯洛往返拉各斯的每日定期航班，表定上午10時10分起飛、航程6小時45分鐘，預定下午5時55分抵達。據Cirium資料，英航全年每天以787-10飛航這條航線；競爭對手包括維珍航空與奈及利亞和平航空，後者由蓋威克機場出發。英航另以波音777每日飛航倫敦希斯洛往返奈及利亞首都阿布加的航線。
